name: United States

election.name: 2026 midterm elections (House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate)

parties.name: Democratic Party
parties.senateNote: Includes 2 independents who caucus with Democrats

system.type: Mostly first-past-the-post in single-member districts (state-run rules vary)
system.elects: All 435 House seats and about one-third of the Senate (35 Senate seats in 2026)
system.eligibility: US citizens 18+ (26th Amendment); further rules set by states

wildFacts.text: In the 2024 presidential election, 65.3% of the citizen voting-age population voted, per the Census Bureau.
In 2024, adults under 30 made up 15% of voters but about 20% of the eligible population.
Gallup found 49% of Americans confident in the honesty of elections in 2026, down from 51% in 2024.

notes: Seats = House of Representatives, AP count (via The Guardian) as of early 4 November 2026: D 228, R 139, 68 uncalled; NBC News shows D 231, R 144, 60 uncalled at about the same time (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results). Senate as of same time: D 54 (incl. 2 independents caucusing with Democrats), R 44, AK and MS uncalled; AP and NBC agree (https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/nov/03/midterm-elections-full-results-senate-house-governor-races ; https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results). Democrats win control of both chambers (AP, NBC). Voting age 18: 26th Amendment https://www.archives.gov/founding-docs/amendments-11-27 . Not compulsory: US absent from International IDEA compulsory-voting list https://www.idea.int/data-tools/data/voter-turnout-database/compulsory-voting . Counting is ongoing, so the map shows the country as a whole. No turnout figure is shown yet.
nationalWinner: Democratic Party (projected control of House and Senate; counting continues)
